cues.en: Mike: Now I'm going to introduce you to something called the receiver operating characteristic, or ROC.
cues.zh: Mike：現在我要介紹所謂的接收者操作特徵，簡稱 ROC。

cues.en: You might think we would be pronouncing this rock, but although I guess that's possible, but everyone just calls these ROC curves.
cues.zh: 你可能以為我們會把它唸成 rock；雖然我想也可以，但大家都直接唸字母，稱它們為 ROC 曲線。

cues.en: I'm gonna start off by talking about the term ROC, what this means and where it comes from, and yeah, and then I'll talk about what the ROC curves mean.
cues.zh: 首先我會談談 ROC 這個詞的意思與由來，再談 ROC 曲線代表什麼。

cues.en: In fact, you already know pretty much everything you need to know about ROC curves from just watching the past several videos in this section, I just haven't been yet using this term.
cues.zh: 事實上，只要看過本節前幾部影片，你就已經知道關於 ROC 曲線幾乎所有需要知道的內容，只是我還沒用這個名稱。

cues.en: So what is receiver operating characteristic mean?
cues.zh: 接收者操作特徵是什麼意思？

cues.en: Well, back in World War II, that's when signal detection theory was really developed in World War II.
cues.zh: 要回到第二次世界大戰，訊號偵測理論正是在二戰期間發展起來的。

cues.en: They were using kind of, you know, what we would today consider relatively primitive sensors and radars for detecting enemy objects in battlefields.
cues.zh: 當時使用一些以今天標準來看相對原始的感測器與雷達，偵測戰場上的敵方物體。

cues.en: This would be planes and tanks and so on.
cues.zh: 例如飛機、坦克等等。

cues.en: And so the way this worked is that the engineers and they would have other experts who were like sitting in a bunker somewhere looking at these radars, trying to read information from the radars
cues.zh: 運作方式是，工程師與其他專家坐在某處的碉堡裡，看著雷達，試著從雷達讀取資訊，

cues.en: when they couldn't actually see what was going on in the real world.
cues.zh: 而他們實際上看不到現實世界裡正在發生什麼。

cues.en: So they had to decide based on the radar information that was available, whether there really was like a tank in the battlefield.
cues.zh: 因此，他們必須根據可取得的雷達資訊，判斷戰場上是否真的有坦克。

cues.en: So these were called the operators.
cues.zh: 這些人就叫操作員。

cues.en: The people who were reading and using these radars were called operators, and they were receiving data.
cues.zh: 讀取與使用這些雷達的人叫操作員，而他們接收資料。

cues.en: So therefore the theory sort of developed for these operators receiving data, and what are their characteristics for identifying tanks
cues.zh: 所以，這套理論逐漸發展成研究這些接收資料的操作員，有什麼樣的特徵，能在坦克

cues.en: when they really are there, or saying that they think there is a tank and there isn't actually a tank, so that's where the term ROC originally comes from.
cues.zh: 確實存在時辨識出來，或是認為有坦克，但實際上沒有；ROC 這個詞最初就是這樣來的。

cues.en: Now, after World War II, signal detection theory was introduced into experimental psychology, and in particular perceptual psychology, trying to understand how people can detect
cues.zh: 二戰之後，訊號偵測理論被引入實驗心理學，尤其是知覺心理學，試著了解人們如何偵測

cues.en: weak sensory events happening in the environment.
cues.zh: 環境中發生的微弱感官事件。

cues.en: That's like the example experiment I gave you towards the beginning of this section.
cues.zh: 就像本節開頭附近，我給你的那個實驗例子。

cues.en: And then, you know, since then over the past decade, signal detection theory is widely used in medicine, and blah, blah, blah, lots of other stuff, and also machine learning and data mining.
cues.zh: 此後，過去十年間，訊號偵測理論廣泛用於醫學，以及其他許多領域，也用於機器學習與資料探勘。

cues.en: Okay, but here is a paper from Duncan Luce.
cues.zh: 這裡有一篇 Duncan Luce 的論文。

cues.en: So Luce is one of the founders of signal detection theory.
cues.zh: Luce 是訊號偵測理論的奠基者之一。

cues.en: He did a lot of early work developing the mathematical theory and the algorithms that we still use today in signal detection theory.
cues.zh: 他做了許多早期工作，發展我們今天在訊號偵測理論中仍使用的數學理論與演算法。

cues.en: Also wrote a couple of textbooks that are fundamental in the signal detection theory literature.
cues.zh: 他也寫了幾本在訊號偵測理論文獻中具有基礎地位的教科書。

cues.en: So this particular paper was written in 1963, and you can see already in the abstract, he's calling these things "isosensitivity curves."
cues.zh: 這篇論文寫於 1963 年，你可以看到，在摘要中，他就把這些稱為「等敏感度曲線」。

cues.en: And then he puts ROC in parentheses, just so, you know, to make sure that people know what he's referring to.
cues.zh: 接著他把 ROC 放在括號中，確保讀者知道他指的是什麼。

cues.en: Later on in this paper and in other papers, he argues that we should be calling these things "isosensitivity curves," because that's, you know, it's a little bit closer to what they're actually showing.
cues.zh: 在這篇論文後面，以及其他論文中，他主張應該稱它們為「等敏感度曲線」，因為這個名稱更貼近實際呈現的內容。

cues.en: ROC is a kind of narrow application of signal detection theory.
cues.zh: ROC 是訊號偵測理論中一個比較狹窄的應用。

cues.en: Anyway, you know how history unfolded over the past 80 years and we, you know, we don't actually use this term, this term, isosensitivity.
cues.zh: 不過，你知道過去 80 年歷史如何發展，我們實際上並沒有使用「等敏感度」這個詞。

cues.en: We use the term ROC, although within, you know, if you are talking to signal detection people, they will know what isosensitivity curves are.
cues.zh: 我們使用 ROC；雖然如果你和訊號偵測領域的人交談，他們會知道等敏感度曲線是什麼。

cues.en: Nonetheless, let's talk about some motivations for drawing isosensitivity curves or ROC curves.
cues.zh: 接著，談談為什麼要畫等敏感度曲線，也就是 ROC 曲線。

cues.en: I'm gonna call this a yes space, and you'll see what this means in a moment.
cues.zh: 我要把這個稱為「是」空間，稍後你就會看到意思。

cues.en: And actually you'll see from these motivations, these are all things that we've discussed before.
cues.zh: 其實，從這些理由你會發現，這些都是我們先前討論過的事情。

cues.en: So we can have identical d-prime values from a variety of different probabilities of hits and probabilities of false alarms,
cues.zh: 不同的命中機率與誤報機率組合，可以得到完全相同的 d′ 值，

cues.en: so this is something we've already discovered.
cues.zh: 這是我們已經發現的事情。

cues.en: And we've also discovered this that hits and false alarms can be separate events.
cues.zh: 我們也發現，命中與誤報可以是分開的事件。

cues.en: We can manipulate these things independently of each other.
cues.zh: 我們可以彼此獨立地操弄它們。

cues.en: So this means that we can generate a two-dimensional space of yeses.
cues.zh: 這表示，我們可以產生一個由「是」構成的二維空間。

cues.en: And the two options for yeses in signal detection theory are hits and false alarms, so this is a yes space.
cues.zh: 訊號偵測理論中，回答「是」的兩種可能是命中與誤報，因此這是「是」空間。

cues.en: Now you already know where this is going because you've already seen these two-dimensional spaces.
cues.zh: 你已經知道接下來要談什麼，因為你看過這些二維空間。

cues.en: This is exactly what we've been looking at in the code, in the past two code videos, so d-prime and also response bias.
cues.zh: 這正是前兩部程式影片中，我們一直在看的內容，也就是 d′ 與反應偏誤。

cues.en: So just as a brief reminder, we have the probability of hits on the Y-axis and the probability of false alarms on the X-axis.
cues.zh: 簡單複習一下，Y 軸是命中機率，X 軸是誤報機率。

cues.en: And then we can draw these ROC curves or isosensitivity curves, which are also called d-prime.
cues.zh: 接著，我們可以畫出 ROC 曲線，也就是等敏感度曲線，也稱為 d′。

cues.en: So that might look something like this.
cues.zh: 看起來可能像這樣。

cues.en: So this would be a d-prime corresponding to one.
cues.zh: 這條對應 d′ 等於 1。

cues.en: So you can see that you get exactly the same d-prime for someone who has 25% hits.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，如果某人的命中率是 25%，會得到完全相同的 d′。

cues.en: So that seems rather low, but only, you know, 5%, or whatever this number is, 5% false alarms versus someone who has 90% hits.
cues.zh: 這看起來很低，但誤報只有 5%，或者這個數值是多少，約 5%；相對地，另一個人的命中率是 90%。

cues.en: So that's really a lot of hits, but they also have a huge number of false alarms.
cues.zh: 他的命中真的很多，但誤報也非常多。

cues.en: So lots of different values, different combinations of hits and false alarms can produce the same d-prime.
cues.zh: 因此，許多不同數值、不同的命中與誤報組合，都可以產生相同的 d′。

cues.en: So here's another example.
cues.zh: 這裡有另一個例子。

cues.en: We have a d-prime of two, and you can kind of imagine filling in this space.
cues.zh: d′ 等於 2，你可以想像在這個空間裡繼續填入曲線。

cues.en: So a d-prime of 1.5 of course is gonna be somewhere in here.
cues.zh: 當然，d′ 等於 1.5 會在這附近。

cues.en: And as the d-prime gets higher and higher, this curve here is getting tighter and tighter, hugging the axis here.
cues.zh: 隨著 d′ 越來越高，這條曲線會越縮越緊，貼近這裡的座標軸。

cues.en: And that should also make sense.
cues.zh: 這也應該很合理。

cues.en: So a really high d-prime means that we have a really high discriminability.
cues.zh: 很高的 d′ 表示辨識能力非常高。

cues.en: So we have very high hits and very few false alarms.
cues.zh: 也就是命中非常多，誤報非常少。

cues.en: Conversely, a d-prime of zero would correspond to this diagonal line here exactly.
cues.zh: 反過來，d′ 為零就恰好對應這條對角線。

cues.en: D-prime of zero is exactly this diagonal line, and that means we have the same number of hits as false alarms.
cues.zh: d′ 為零恰好就是這條對角線，表示命中次數與誤報次數相同。

cues.en: So that would be the case where, you know, you're just saying yes all the time, so you get a bunch of hits, but you also have the same number of false alarms.
cues.zh: 例如，你一直回答「是」，就會得到許多命中，但也會有同樣多的誤報。

cues.en: So these are the d-prime isosensitivity curves, aka ROC curves.
cues.zh: 這些就是 d′ 等敏感度曲線，也就是 ROC 曲線。

cues.en: And now of course you know that we can also draw the response bias in the same space.
cues.zh: 當然，你也知道，我們可以在相同的空間裡畫出反應偏誤。

cues.en: So again, we can have a response bias for the same response bias for many different values of hits and false alarms,
cues.zh: 同樣地，許多不同的命中與誤報值，可以有相同的反應偏誤，

cues.en: and these go kind of orthogonal to the d-primes.
cues.zh: 而這些線與 d′ 大致正交。

cues.en: So this would be a positive response bias.
cues.zh: 這是正的反應偏誤。

cues.en: This would be a negative response bias.
cues.zh: 這是負的反應偏誤。

cues.en: And remember, with d-prime, we don't really expect any values below zero.
cues.zh: 記得，對 d′ 而言，我們並不太預期有小於零的值。

cues.en: We don't expect d-prime values below zero, but response bias certainly could go either way.
cues.zh: 我們不預期 d′ 小於零，但反應偏誤當然可能往任一方向。

cues.en: So we can expect that these lines could be drawn in real data.
cues.zh: 因此，在真實資料中，我們可能畫出這些線。

cues.en: These lines could be drawn anywhere in this space here.
cues.zh: 這些線可能出現在這個空間的任何位置。

cues.en: So that's the whole idea of these ROC curves or isosensitivity curves.
cues.zh: 這就是 ROC 曲線或等敏感度曲線的整體概念。

cues.en: They reveal the d-prime values and response bias values that have paired hits and false alarm rates.
cues.zh: 它們呈現成對的命中率與誤報率所對應的 d′ 與反應偏誤值。

cues.en: So most of this stuff you've already seen in code, the main thing that we haven't done yet is actually draw these lines into these two dimensional yes spaces,
cues.zh: 這些內容大多已經在程式中看過，唯一還沒做的，是真正在這些二維的「是」空間中畫出這些線，

cues.en: and that's what we're going to do in the next video.
cues.zh: 下一部影片就會來做。
